<x_0.0742><y_0.0266>e litre or cubic decimetre = 10 decilitres = 100 centilitres
= 027052 Brit. cubic inches; and 50 litres are nearly 11 Brit.
Also 100 litres = 10 decalitres = 1 hectolitre = 2·751207
bushels; and 32 hectolitres are nearly equal to 11 Brit.
quters, and 100 hectolitres = 10 kilolitres or cubic metres = 1
alitre = 34-300086 Brit. quarters.<x_0.957><y_0.0984><class_Text>

<x_0.0752><y_0.0914>te gramme is a weight equal that of 1 cubic centimetre of
at its maximum density. It contains 10 decigrammes = 100
grammes = 15·434 troy grains; and 1000 grammes = 100
grammes = 10 hectogrammes = 1 kilograme = 2·679514 lbs.
r = 2·204857 lbs. avoird. Also 100 kilogrammes = 10 myria-
grmes = 1 metrical quintal = 220·486 lbs. avoird.; and 10
tails = weight of a cubic metre of water = 1 millier or marine
to = 19 Brit. ewt. 2 qrs. 20 lbs. 13·75 oz.<x_0.958><y_0.1828><class_Text>

<x_0.0762><y_0.1766>ne _Syttime Uncl_, or Binary System, of the French, was intro-
d in 1812, for the accommodation of retail trade, to make a
of compromise with the common people, who showed an irre-
oleable aversion to the innovations of the metrical or decimal
com. It has the metrical standards for its basis; but their
diions, &c. instead of being decimal, are chiefly binary, that is,
proceed principally by continually halving or doubling some
these standards, though partly according to other divisions of
hold system; and instead of the metrical vocabulary, the names
ecient weights and measures are employed, annexing the term
ul to each. Thus, the toise usuelle = 2 metres = 78·74158
b. inches. The pied usuel is one sixth of the toise, and is sub-
ided into twelfths or inches, &c. The aune usuelle = 12 deci-
mes = 1·2 metre = 47·2449 Brit. inches. The litron usuel =
re = 1·7608 Brit. pint. The Boisseau usuel is one eighth of
hectolitre, and = 2·7512 Brit. gallons. The livre usuelle is
the kilogramme, and = 1·10243 lb. avoird. The halves, quar-
to, eighths, &c. of the most of the above are also in use. A
mary of the ancient French system will be found in the pre-
ceg part of this article.<x_0.96><y_0.393><class_Text>

<x_0.0889><y_0.3891>_rankfort on the Maisuc._—Of the weights, 128 drachmes = 32
les = 2 marks = 1 heavy lb. = 1·1143 lb. avoird. The light lb-
similarly divided, but only = 1·0318 lb. avoird., so that 108 of
light lbs. make only 100 of the heavy or centmer weight. The
Cogne mark, here reckoned = 3611 grains troy, is used for gold
silver. The Frankfort foot contains 11·42 Brit. inches, and
cell 21·54. The Brabant ell is generally used for Dutch goods,
the Paris aune for French. Eighty old or 90 new mass (each
schoppen) are equal to 20 viertels = 1 ohm = 31·57 Brit. gall.;
a 16 sechters = 8 metzen = 4 simmers = 1 malter or achtel =
Brit. bushels.<x_0.9609><y_0.5078><class_Text>

<x_0.0898><y_0.5055>cross.—There are two sorts of pounds, the peso sottile lb., and
peso grossolb. The latter is a tenth part heavier than the for-
n, so that the cantaro of 100 lbs. peso sottile = 69·89 lbs. avoird.,
the cantaro of 100 lbs. peso grosso = 76·88. The latter is
for bulky commodities, and the former for gold, silver, and
articles of small bulk. The palmo = 9·725 Brit. inches, and
33 palmi = 1 braccio. The canna is of three sorts: the canna
pola used by tradesmen = 9 palmi, the canna grossa of the mer-
ants = 12 palmi, and the custom-house canna = 10 palmi. Of
measure, 96 gombette = 8 quarti = 1 mina = 3·31 Brit. bush-
Also 100 pints = 2 barili = 1 mezzarola of wine = 32·67
t. gall.; and 64 quateroni = 4 quarti = 1 oil barile = 14·23
t. gall.<x_0.9736><y_0.6469><class_Text>

<x_0.0928><y_0.6438>Gressary.—Considerable diversity of weights and measures is
found in the various states into which this extensive coun-
is divided, and the most important of them will be found
iced separately. But not a few of their standards, though dif-
ng in amount, are similar in their multiples and subdivisions.
the weights, 1024 hellers = 312 pfennings = 128 quentins =
loths = 16 ounces = 2 marks = 1 commercial lb.; and 5760
in = 288 scruples = 96 drams = 12 oz. = 1 apothecaries' lb.;
4352 eschen = 512 hellers = 256 pfennings = 64 quentins =
loths = 8 oz. = 1 Cologne mark = 3608 grains troy. By this
and silver are weighed ; and the fineness of gold is expressed
24th parts or carats as in Britain, but the fineness of silver by
parts. For jewellery there is a carat of 3·171 grs. troy. Of
measures, 144 inches = 12 feet = 6 cells = 2 clafters = 4 ruthe.
e Rhinland foot used by surveyors = 12·36 Brit. inches; the
g mile = 10,126 Brit. yds., the short mile = 6859, and the
graphical mile = 8101 Brit. yds. The Rhinland morgen of
d = 10,185 Brit. sq. yds.<x_0.9795><y_0.8383><class_Text>

<x_0.1055><y_0.8328>Gibraltar.—Besides the British standards, the following Spanish
also used: The arroba = 26 lbs. avoird.; the quintal = 100
= 101·75 lbs. avourd.; the corn fanega = 1·55 Brit. bushel;
pipe of 117 gallons = 105 Brit. gall.; the liquid arroba =
7 Brit. gall.; and the wine gallon = 1·094 Brit. gall.
Go.—The same as in Portugal, except that the candy of 20
onds = 495 lbs. avoird. This, in the measurement of grain, is
koed to be nearly 14 Winchester bushels.<x_0.9775><y_0.925><class_Text>
